intro.TrustedMarkup:
The command line is a record type, and cli writes its parser and help.

import { cli } from "std/cli"
import { parseServe, helpServe } from cli("./serve")

cli is a gen fn that reflects a module of type declarations and returns a module exporting, for every exported record type, parse<Name>(argv) -> Validation<Name> and help<Name>() -> String. The compiler knows nothing about command lines. The mapping is a rule over the declaration, never an attribute:

| field type | surface | missing | |---|---|---| | Bool | --verbose | false | | Option<T> | --host <value> | None | | bare T | --port <value> | an Issue at path port | | Array<String> | the positionals, at most one field | empty |

  • The long name is the field name in kebab-case: dryRun is --dry-run.
  • The short name is the first byte of the field name, taken in declaration order and skipped on collision. -h is reserved for --help.
  • An unknown option is an Issue: unlike std/args, a spec exists.
  • A value is validated by construction: --port 99999 reaches Port?(99999), and its None becomes an Issue worded from that type's Schema, so the parser and the program run one check.
  • An option's help text is the /// above its named type (TypeInfo.schema.doc), so a documented option needs a named type.
  • --help is a question about argv, not a value in the record: ask it with wantsHelp(argv) before parsing.

A field is Bool, Int64, String, a validated type over Int64 or String, an Option of those, or one Array<String> for the positionals. Anything else fails the generation with a sentence naming the field.

Inspect the synthesized module with: vyrn emit-gen <file>

sig.TrustedMarkup: type CliHit = { field: String, value: String }

prose.TrustedMarkup: One option seen in argv: the field it fills, and the text it carried ("" for a flag).

sig.TrustedMarkup: type CliRead = { hits: Array<CliHit>, free: Array<String>, issues: Array<Issue>, }

prose.TrustedMarkup: What one walk of argv found: the options, the free arguments, and the problems with the argv itself (unknown option, missing value). The generated parser raises the problems with a value.
Whether --help or -h appears before a -- terminator. Ask it before parsing: a program asked for help has not given the required options.
Emits a module exporting parse<Name> and help<Name> for every exported record type module declares.
